method: Whole md-scheduler.c/h read with Git blob verification; static analysis.
findings: Device workers keep unsorted and sorted queues, process quota per pass and resubmit while device reference count positive. Deferred callbacks must requeue work and retain device references themselves.

finish waits until device table empty then joins worker pool; no timeout or explicit cancellation path in this scheduler. Completion depends on balanced external references and callbacks making progress.
Queue push allocates task without queue-length or byte admission limit; read-buffer budget does not bound scheduler backlog.
Freshly sorted incoming tasks are concatenated before old sorted tasks rather than merged into a globally sorted sequence; elevator locality applies to batches, not whole queued set.
Device table keys convert dev_t through GINT_TO_POINTER. Wider device identifiers need platform-specific validation before claiming key collisions.

Header callback names task type but implementation passes task_data; quota documentation suggests decrement amount while worker counts any nonzero result as one. Internal caller behavior must follow implementation.
Startup uses configured threads_per_disk and max_threads; zero/negative argument validation is external. No benchmark evidence collected.
limits: No concurrent stress tests or original runtime execution; suspected scheduling/lifetime hazards not proven reachable.
No rrrah edits/tests; native pHash deferred; global count150/500.
